solvency_ii_scr_credit_risk.text: `solvency_ii_scr_market_risk` answers "how much capital is needed for market risk?" It takes a charge for each market sub-module (interest rate, equity, property, spread, currency, concentration) and combines them with a prescribed correlation matrix using a square-root formula, so diversification between sub-modules is reflected. `solvency_ii_scr_credit_risk` answers "how much capital is needed for counterparty default on Type 1 exposures?" Instead of ready-made charges, it takes `exposures`, `loss_given_default` and `default_probabilities` per counterparty, and builds the loss variability (sigma) from those. It then applies the prescribed multiplier on sigma, capped at total loss given default. Its sigma covers only the intra-counterparty variance term, so its result can understate the full regulatory figure.

explain.text: `solvency_ii_scr_market_risk` (Solvency II SCR Market Risk) combines the capital charges for the market risk sub-modules (interest rate, equity, property, spread, currency and concentration) into a single market risk SCR. You pass in the charge for each sub-module as `sub_module_charges` and the prescribed correlation matrix as `correlation_matrix`. It applies the standard-formula square-root aggregation, SCR = sqrt(s' Corr s), from Delegated Regulation 2015/35 Art. 164. Because the correlations are below perfect, the total reflects diversification between the sub-modules. You can also supply `sub_module_names` to label the diversification report.

when.text:
Use Solvency II SCR Market Risk (`solvency_ii_scr_market_risk`) when you need the market-risk capital charge under the standard formula. It fits in these cases:

- You already have capital charges for each market sub-module (interest rate, equity, property, spread, currency, concentration) and want them combined into one market-risk figure.
- You need aggregation that uses the prescribed correlation matrix, so diversification between sub-modules is reflected through the square-root formula in Delegated Regulation 2015/35 Art. 164.
- You want a diversification report with readable labels, which you can get by passing `sub_module_names`.
- You are working with the standard formula rather than an internal model.

For a different need, `solvency_ii_scr_credit_risk` covers Solvency II SCR counterparty default (credit) risk, Type 1 exposures.
